q-antike-griechenland-39#explanation: Eratosthenes compared the sun's angle at Syene and Alexandria and deduced the Earth's circumference from it. He was head of the famous Library of Alexandria.
q-antike-griechenland-40#question: Who was allowed to take part in decisions in the assembly of democratic Athens?
q-antike-griechenland-40#explanation: Women, metics and slaves were excluded from politics, so only a small part of the population had a say. The assembly made the most important decisions of the polis.
q-antike-griechenland-41#question: What did the Greeks add when they adopted the Phoenician alphabet?
q-antike-griechenland-41#explanation: The Phoenician alphabet had only consonants; with vowel letters the first complete alphabet was created. It passed to the Romans via the Etruscans.
q-antike-griechenland-42#question: Which dynasty ruled Syria, Mesopotamia and Iran after the Wars of the Diadochi?
q-antike-griechenland-42#explanation: The empire went back to Alexander's general Seleucus. The Ptolemies, by contrast, ruled Egypt, the Antigonids Macedon and the Attalids Pergamon.
q-antike-griechenland-43#question: In honour of which god were the tragedies performed in Athens?
q-antike-griechenland-43#explanation: Tragedy grew out of choral songs for Dionysus. At his festival, the Dionysia, three poets competed for victory every year.
q-antike-griechenland-44#question: Which tragedian wrote “Antigone” and “Oedipus the King”?
q-antike-griechenland-44#explanation: Sophocles introduced the third actor to the stage. His plays show people caught between divine law, the state and fate.
q-antike-griechenland-45#question: Who seized lasting power in Athens around 546 BC and ruled as tyrant?
q-antike-griechenland-45#explanation: Peisistratus left Solon's laws in place, supported small farmers and staged great festivals such as the Dionysia. His son Hippias was driven out in 510 BC.
q-antike-griechenland-46#question: Which philosopher is associated with the saying “I know that I know nothing”?
q-antike-griechenland-46#explanation: In conversation, Socrates exposed his fellow citizens' false knowledge. Since he wrote nothing himself, we know him mainly from Plato's dialogues.
q-antike-griechenland-47#question: Which philosopher is the author of the Allegory of the Cave?
q-antike-griechenland-47#explanation: In the Republic, Plato depicts people who see only shadows on a cave wall, illustrating his theory of Forms. Around 387 BC he founded the Academy.
q-antike-griechenland-48#explanation: The Parthenon was built from 447 BC, and the Peloponnesian War began in 431. Socrates died in 399, and Alexander set out for Asia in 334 BC.
q-antike-griechenland-49#question: Which mathematician summarised the knowledge of his time in the “Elements”, the textbook of geometry?
q-antike-griechenland-49#explanation: Euclid taught in Alexandria around 300 BC and derived every theorem from a few definitions and axioms. The Elements were used as a school textbook into the 20th century.
q-antike-griechenland-50#question: Which Greek city did the Romans destroy in 146 BC, making Greece part of their empire?
q-antike-griechenland-50#explanation: With this Rome crushed the revolt of the Achaean League. Yet the Romans adopted the art, literature and philosophy of the Greeks.
q-antike-griechenland-51#question: In which battle in 338 BC was the alliance of Athens and Thebes, forged by Demosthenes, defeated by Philip II?
q-antike-griechenland-51#explanation: The victory at Chaeronea made Macedon the dominant power in Greece. Demosthenes had previously warned against Philip in his Philippics.
q-antike-griechenland-52#question: What happened to the loser of an ostracism vote in Athens?
q-antike-griechenland-52#choices.2: He had to leave Athens for ten years
q-antike-griechenland-52#explanation: The exile kept his property and citizenship; the procedure was meant to prevent a new tyranny. Citizens scratched names onto pottery shards, called ostraka in Greek.
q-asiatische-grossreiche-01#question: What title did the Mongol Temüjin receive at an assembly of the tribes in 1206?
q-asiatische-grossreiche-01#explanation: In 1206 the Mongol tribes proclaimed Temüjin Genghis Khan, the universal ruler.
q-asiatische-grossreiche-02#question: Which Mughal emperor had the Taj Mahal built as a tomb for his wife?
q-asiatische-grossreiche-02#explanation: From 1632 Shah Jahan had the Taj Mahal built in Agra for his late wife Mumtaz Mahal.
q-asiatische-grossreiche-03#question: In which city is the Forbidden City of the Ming and Qing emperors located?
q-asiatische-grossreiche-03#explanation: The Yongle emperor had the Forbidden City built in Beijing from 1406 to 1420; the city became the capital in 1421.
q-asiatische-grossreiche-04#question: Which script did King Sejong have developed in Korea in the 15th century?
q-asiatische-grossreiche-04#explanation: Sejong had the Hangeul alphabet developed in 1443 and promulgated in 1446.
q-asiatische-grossreiche-05#question: Which admiral led seven Chinese fleets as far as East Africa between 1405 and 1433?
q-asiatische-grossreiche-05#explanation: Zheng He commanded seven fleet voyages across the Indian Ocean on behalf of the Ming.
q-asiatische-grossreiche-06#question: Through which battle in 1600 did Tokugawa Ieyasu secure supremacy in Japan?
q-asiatische-grossreiche-06#explanation: With his victory at Sekigahara in 1600, Ieyasu laid the foundation for the Tokugawa shogunate.
q-asiatische-grossreiche-07#question: Which branch of faith did Shah Ismail I make the state religion of Persia after 1501?
q-asiatische-grossreiche-07#explanation: Ismail I made the Twelver branch of Shiism the state religion, which still shapes Iran today.
q-asiatische-grossreiche-08#question: What did the Treaty of Nerchinsk of 1689 settle?
q-asiatische-grossreiche-08#choices.0: The closing of Japan to Europe
q-asiatische-grossreiche-08#choices.1: The end of the Imjin War in Korea
q-asiatische-grossreiche-08#choices.2: The partition of the Mughal Empire
q-asiatische-grossreiche-08#choices.3: The border between Russia and Qing China
q-asiatische-grossreiche-08#explanation: At Nerchinsk, Russia and China fixed their border on the Amur by treaty for the first time.
q-asiatische-grossreiche-09#question: Which city did Shah Abbas I make the Safavid capital in 1598?
q-asiatische-grossreiche-09#explanation: Abbas I moved the capital to Isfahan in 1598 and had it developed lavishly.
q-asiatische-grossreiche-10#question: Who founded the Mughal Empire in 1526 with his victory at the Battle of Panipat?
q-asiatische-grossreiche-10#explanation: At Panipat Babur defeated Ibrahim Lodi, the last Sultan of Delhi, and founded the Mughal Empire.
q-asiatische-grossreiche-11#question: Which Hindu empire with its capital near Hampi dominated southern India from the 14th century?
q-asiatische-grossreiche-11#explanation: Vijayanagara was founded around 1336 and dominated southern India until its defeat at Talikota in 1565.
q-asiatische-grossreiche-12#question: What contributed decisively to the failure of the Mongol invasion of Japan in 1281?
q-asiatische-grossreiche-12#choices.0: A plague epidemic in the Mongol army
q-asiatische-grossreiche-12#choices.2: A typhoon that destroyed much of the fleet
q-asiatische-grossreiche-12#choices.3: An alliance between Japan and Korea
q-asiatische-grossreiche-12#explanation: In 1281 a typhoon destroyed much of the invasion fleet; the Japanese called it kamikaze, the divine wind.
q-asiatische-grossreiche-13#question: Which empire is considered the largest contiguous land empire in history?
q-asiatische-grossreiche-13#choices.3: The empire of Alexander the Great
q-asiatische-grossreiche-13#explanation: In the 13th century Genghis Khan and his successors ruled an area from Korea to Eastern Europe. The British Empire was later larger, but scattered across the oceans.
q-asiatische-grossreiche-14#question: In which city did Minamoto no Yoritomo establish Japan's first warrior government in 1192?
q-asiatische-grossreiche-14#explanation: Yoritomo set up his shogunate in Kamakura, far from the imperial court in Kyoto. Edo, today's Tokyo, became the centre of power only under the Tokugawa.
q-asiatische-grossreiche-15#question: Which grandson of Genghis Khan conquered the Russian principalities and founded the Golden Horde?
q-asiatische-grossreiche-15#explanation: From 1237 Batu led the Mongol invasion of Eastern Europe and then founded the Golden Horde with its capital Sarai on the Volga. Hulagu, by contrast, conquered Persia and Baghdad.
q-asiatische-grossreiche-16#question: What does the term Pax Mongolica refer to?
q-asiatische-grossreiche-16#choices.0: A peace treaty between the Mongols and Japan
q-asiatische-grossreiche-16#choices.1: The law code of Genghis Khan
q-asiatische-grossreiche-16#choices.2: A period of relatively safe travel and trade under Mongol rule
q-asiatische-grossreiche-16#choices.3: The conversion of the Mongols to Buddhism
q-asiatische-grossreiche-16#explanation: In the 13th and 14th centuries merchants, envoys and missionaries could travel from China to Eastern Europe under Mongol protection. A network of post stations made the journey easier.
q-asiatische-grossreiche-17#question: Which dynasty did Kublai Khan proclaim in China in 1271?
q-asiatische-grossreiche-17#explanation: Kublai Khan gave his rule a Chinese dynastic name and conquered the Song empire by 1279. The Yuan were driven out by the Ming in 1368.
q-asiatische-grossreiche-18#question: Which Venetian travelled to the court of Kublai Khan in the 13th century?
q-asiatische-grossreiche-18#explanation: Marco Polo set out in 1271 with his father and uncle and lived for about two decades in Kublai Khan's empire. His travel account shaped Europe's image of China for centuries.
q-asiatische-grossreiche-19#choices.0: An empress of the Ming dynasty
q-asiatische-grossreiche-19#choices.1: The mother of Kublai Khan, who helped steer the policy of the Mongol Empire
q-asiatische-grossreiche-19#choices.2: A poet at the Joseon court
q-asiatische-grossreiche-19#choices.3: The wife of Timur and mistress of Samarkand
q-asiatische-grossreiche-19#explanation: Sorghaghtani Beki secured power in the Mongol Empire for her sons Möngke, Kublai and Hulagu. She promoted trade and agriculture and protected different religions.
q-asiatische-grossreiche-20#question: Which epidemic also spread west in the 14th century along the trade routes of the Mongol Empire?
q-asiatische-grossreiche-20#explanation: The plague spread from Central Asia along caravan and sea routes and reached Europe in 1347. There it killed about a third of the population.
q-asiatische-grossreiche-21#question: In which country was the oldest surviving book printed with movable metal type produced in 1377?
q-asiatische-grossreiche-21#explanation: The Jikji was produced at the Korean monastery of Heungdeoksa, about 80 years before Gutenberg's Bible. The surviving copy is today held by the National Library of France.
q-asiatische-grossreiche-22#question: Which general founded the Joseon dynasty in Korea in 1392?
q-asiatische-grossreiche-22#explanation: Yi Seong-gye overthrew the kingdom of Goryeo and made Hanyang, today's Seoul, the capital. Wang Geon, by contrast, had founded Goryeo in the 10th century.
q-asiatische-grossreiche-23#question: Besides the Hangeul script, what did King Sejong have developed?
q-asiatische-grossreiche-23#explanation: Sejong supported scholars and inventors such as Jang Yeong-sil, who built rain gauges, sundials and water clocks. The rainfall measurements helped plan harvests and taxes.
q-asiatische-grossreiche-24#question: Which dynasty expanded the Great Wall into its present form of stone and brick?
q-asiatische-grossreiche-24#explanation: After Mongol attacks reached the outskirts of Beijing, the Ming strengthened the border fortifications, above all in the 16th century. Older walls were mostly made of rammed earth.
q-asiatische-grossreiche-25#question: How did the Ming court act after Zheng He's voyages ended in 1433?
q-asiatische-grossreiche-25#choices.0: It founded trading colonies in East Africa
q-asiatische-grossreiche-25#choices.1: It stopped the great expeditions and restricted maritime trade
q-asiatische-grossreiche-25#choices.2: It sent a fleet as far as Europe
q-asiatische-grossreiche-25#choices.3: It conquered the islands of Japan
q-asiatische-grossreiche-25#explanation: After 1433 the court regarded the costly expeditions as wasteful and concentrated on defending the north against the Mongols. Private maritime trade long remained banned or heavily restricted.
q-asiatische-grossreiche-26#question: What did Timur's grandson Ulugh Beg have built in Samarkand?
q-asiatische-grossreiche-26#choices.1: A canal to the Caspian Sea
q-asiatische-grossreiche-26#explanation: The observatory was built from 1424; its star catalogue was among the most accurate before the invention of the telescope. Ulugh Beg was himself an astronomer and mathematician.
q-asiatische-grossreiche-27#question: Which city did Timur make the capital of his empire?
q-asiatische-grossreiche-27#explanation: Timur brought artists and craftsmen from conquered cities to Samarkand and adorned it with splendid mosques and tombs. Delhi and Baghdad, by contrast, he plundered.
q-asiatische-grossreiche-28#question: Whom did Lê Lợi drive out of Đại Việt in 1428?
q-asiatische-grossreiche-28#choices.0: The Chinese troops of the Ming
q-asiatische-grossreiche-28#explanation: The Ming had occupied Vietnam in 1407; after a ten-year uprising Lê Lợi forced their withdrawal. He founded the Lê dynasty, which ruled Vietnam for a long time.
q-asiatische-grossreiche-29#question: Which people abandoned their old capital Angkor after an attack from Ayutthaya around 1431?
q-asiatische-grossreiche-29#explanation: The Khmer kings moved their seat south to the area of present-day Phnom Penh. Angkor thus lost its role as a centre of power in Southeast Asia; Ayutthaya was the capital of the Thai.
q-asiatische-grossreiche-30#question: Why did Malacca become one of Asia's most important ports around 1400?
q-asiatische-grossreiche-30#choices.0: Because of its location on the strait between the Indian Ocean and the South China Sea
q-asiatische-grossreiche-30#choices.1: Because of rich gold mines in its hinterland
q-asiatische-grossreiche-30#choices.2: Because it was the capital of the Ming emperors
q-asiatische-grossreiche-30#explanation: Ships between India and China had to pass through the Strait of Malacca and wait for the monsoon to change. The sultan of Malacca adopted Islam, which spread further from there.
q-asiatische-grossreiche-31#question: Which religion became dominant in Siam, Burma and Cambodia during this period?
q-asiatische-grossreiche-31#explanation: Monks and kings spread Theravada Buddhism, which remains the majority religion in Thailand, Myanmar and Cambodia today. Twelver Shiism, by contrast, became the state religion in Persia.
q-asiatische-grossreiche-32#choices.2: Capture of Beijing by the Manchus
q-asiatische-grossreiche-32#explanation: The Ming dynasty was founded in 1368, Hangeul promulgated in 1446, the Mughal Empire founded in 1526 and Beijing taken by the Manchus in 1644. The Ming thus ruled China for almost 300 years.
q-asiatische-grossreiche-33#question: Which religion did Guru Nanak found in the Punjab around 1500?
q-asiatische-grossreiche-33#explanation: Guru Nanak taught belief in one God and rejected caste distinctions. Jainism, by contrast, is more than 2,000 years older.
q-asiatische-grossreiche-34#question: What is the Mughal emperor Akbar particularly known for?
q-asiatische-grossreiche-34#choices.0: Religious tolerance and religious debates at his court
q-asiatische-grossreiche-34#explanation: Akbar abolished the poll tax on non-Muslims, integrated Hindu princes and had scholars of different religions debate with each other. The Taj Mahal was built by his grandson Shah Jahan; the empire was founded by his grandfather Babur.
q-asiatische-grossreiche-35#question: What did the mansab system determine in the Mughal Empire?
q-asiatische-grossreiche-35#choices.0: The customs duties for European merchants
q-asiatische-grossreiche-35#choices.1: An official's rank, pay and the number of horsemen he had to provide
q-asiatische-grossreiche-35#choices.3: The inheritance rights of women at court
q-asiatische-grossreiche-35#explanation: Akbar gave each mansabdar a rank that determined his income and his duty to provide cavalry. The ranks were not hereditary, which allowed the ruler to control the nobility.
q-asiatische-grossreiche-36#question: Which woman effectively held power in the Mughal Empire alongside the emperor Jahangir?
q-asiatische-grossreiche-36#explanation: Nur Jahan had coins minted in her name and issued orders while Jahangir withdrew. Mumtaz Mahal, by contrast, was the wife of Shah Jahan, for whom the Taj Mahal was built.
q-asiatische-grossreiche-37#question: Who were the Qizilbash in the Safavid Empire?
q-asiatische-grossreiche-37#choices.0: The bodyguard of the Mughal emperors
q-asiatische-grossreiche-37#choices.3: Turkmen cavalry warriors on whom the Safavids relied
q-asiatische-grossreiche-37#explanation: The Qizilbash, "redheads" after their red headgear, helped Ismail I to power. Abbas I later curbed their influence with new troops of slave soldiers.
q-asiatische-grossreiche-38#question: Which city did the Mughals and Safavids long fight over?
q-asiatische-grossreiche-38#explanation: Kandahar in present-day Afghanistan lay on the important trade route between India and Persia and changed hands several times. The Safavids fought over Baghdad, by contrast, with the Ottomans.
q-asiatische-grossreiche-39#question: What was the title of the military commander who actually ruled Japan in place of the emperor?
q-asiatische-grossreiche-39#explanation: The emperor (Tennō) remained a religious figurehead in Kyoto while the shogun ran the country. The daimyō were the regional lords and the samurai the warrior class.
q-asiatische-grossreiche-40#question: Which lord began the unification of Japan with a victory at Okehazama in 1560?
q-asiatische-grossreiche-40#explanation: Oda Nobunaga defeated a far larger army and later used firearms on a large scale. After his death in 1582, Hideyoshi and Ieyasu continued the unification.
q-asiatische-grossreiche-41#question: What was Toyotomi Hideyoshi's aim in attacking Korea in 1592?
q-asiatische-grossreiche-41#choices.2: Driving the Portuguese out of Asia
q-asiatische-grossreiche-41#choices.3: Control of the silk trade with Europe
q-asiatische-grossreiche-41#explanation: Korea was meant to be only the route to conquering the Ming empire. Korean resistance, Yi Sun-sin's fleet and Ming troops made the plan fail.
q-asiatische-grossreiche-42#question: What does the Japanese term sakoku refer to?
q-asiatische-grossreiche-42#choices.2: The art of the tea ceremony
q-asiatische-grossreiche-42#choices.3: Japan's closing of the country to the outside
q-asiatische-grossreiche-42#explanation: From 1639 to 1854 foreigners could hardly enter and Japanese were not allowed to leave the country. Foreign trade was confined to a few partners, above all the Dutch and Chinese at Nagasaki.
q-asiatische-grossreiche-43#question: What did the Tokugawa shoguns oblige the regional lords (daimyō) to do?
q-asiatische-grossreiche-43#choices.1: Send their sons to study in China
q-asiatische-grossreiche-43#choices.2: Equip a fleet for maritime trade every year
q-asiatische-grossreiche-43#choices.3: Reside in Edo in alternate years and leave their families there
q-asiatische-grossreiche-43#explanation: The system of alternate attendance cost the daimyō a great deal of money and kept their families as hostages in the capital. In this way the Tokugawa secured peace for over two centuries.
q-asiatische-grossreiche-44#question: Which class stood at the top of Japan's four classes in the Edo period?
q-asiatische-grossreiche-44#explanation: Only samurai were allowed to carry swords, and they increasingly served as officials. Merchants formally ranked lowest but often became very wealthy.
q-asiatische-grossreiche-45#question: Which poetic form did Matsuo Bashō turn into an art form of its own?
q-asiatische-grossreiche-45#explanation: In the 17th century Bashō condensed impressions of nature into short verses of 5, 7 and 5 syllables. His poem about the old pond and the jumping frog is world-famous.
q-asiatische-grossreiche-46#question: Which people conquered Beijing in 1644 and founded the Qing dynasty?
q-asiatische-grossreiche-46#explanation: After rebels had overthrown the Ming, the Manchus from the north-east entered Beijing. The Qing remained China's last imperial dynasty until 1912.
q-asiatische-grossreiche-47#question: What were the Eight Banners of the Manchus?
q-asiatische-grossreiche-47#choices.0: The flags of China's eight tributary states
q-asiatische-grossreiche-47#choices.1: Military units to which all Manchu families were assigned
q-asiatische-grossreiche-47#choices.2: Eight levels of the civil service career
q-asiatische-grossreiche-47#choices.3: Eight provinces into which China was divided
q-asiatische-grossreiche-47#explanation: The banners, named after the colours of their flags, conquered China in 1644 and afterwards formed a privileged garrison force. Mongol and Chinese banners were later created as well.
q-asiatische-grossreiche-48#question: Which emperor reigned the longest in Chinese history?
q-asiatische-grossreiche-48#explanation: The Kangxi emperor reigned for 61 years, from 1661 to 1722. His grandson Qianlong abdicated after 60 years so as not to exceed his grandfather's reign.
q-asiatische-grossreiche-49#question: Which crops from the Americas contributed to China's strong population growth?
q-asiatische-grossreiche-49#explanation: The new plants also thrived on slopes and poor soils where rice would not grow. By around 1800 China had about 300 million inhabitants.
q-asiatische-grossreiche-50#question: From where did especially large amounts of silver flow into China from the 16th century?
q-asiatische-grossreiche-50#explanation: Spanish silver from the Americas reached China via Manila, along with silver from Japanese mines. China demanded payment in silver for silk, porcelain and tea and increasingly collected taxes in silver.
q-asiatische-grossreiche-51#question: Which commodity drew Russian traders and Cossacks into Siberia?
q-asiatische-grossreiche-51#explanation: The precious fur of the sable was in great demand in Europe and Asia. In pursuit of it, the Russians pushed on as far as the Pacific.
q-asiatische-grossreiche-52#question: What did the British embassy under Lord Macartney seek to achieve in China in 1793?
q-asiatische-grossreiche-52#choices.1: An alliance against the Russian Empire
q-asiatische-grossreiche-52#choices.2: Chinese help in the war against France
q-asiatische-grossreiche-52#choices.3: Better trading conditions and a permanent mission in Beijing
q-asiatische-grossreiche-52#explanation: The Qianlong emperor refused and declared that China had no need of British goods. The rebuff foreshadowed the conflicts of the 19th century.
q-asien-altertum-01#question: Who founded the Persian Empire of the Achaemenids around 550 BC?
q-asien-altertum-01#explanation: Cyrus II defeated the Medes and went on to conquer Lydia and Babylon; Darius and Xerxes were later Great Kings.
q-asien-altertum-02#question: Which teaching did Siddhartha Gautama proclaim in northern India?
q-asien-altertum-02#explanation: As the Buddha, the Awakened One, Siddhartha Gautama became the founder of Buddhism.
q-asien-altertum-03#question: What, among other things, did Qin Shi Huang standardize after the unification of China in 221 BC?
q-asien-altertum-03#explanation: The First Emperor introduced uniform characters, coins, measures, weights and axle widths in order to hold the empire together.
q-asien-altertum-04#question: Which invention is attributed to the Chinese court official Cai Lun in the year 105?
q-asien-altertum-04#explanation: In 105 Cai Lun described an improved process for making paper from bark, hemp and rags.
q-asien-altertum-05#question: Which mathematical innovation arose in India in the time of the Gupta Empire?
q-asien-altertum-05#explanation: Indian mathematicians of the Gupta period developed the decimal system with the digit zero, which reached Europe by way of the Arab world.
q-asien-altertum-06#question: Under which king was Angkor Wat built in the 12th century?
q-asien-altertum-06#explanation: The Khmer king Suryavarman II had Angkor Wat built as a temple to Vishnu and as his own tomb.
q-asien-altertum-07#question: To which sage is the Tao Te Ching, the foundational text of Daoism, attributed?
q-asien-altertum-07#explanation: The Tao Te Ching is regarded as the work of the legendary Laozi; Zhuangzi was a later Daoist thinker, while Confucius and Mengzi represented Confucianism.
q-asien-altertum-08#question: What is the name of the work by the strategist Sun Tzu from the period of the Warring States?
q-asien-altertum-08#explanation: Sun Tzu's Art of War, in thirteen chapters, teaches that the best victory is won without a battle.
q-asien-altertum-09#question: What was remarkable about the reign of Wu Zetian from 690 to 705?
q-asien-altertum-09#choices.0: She was the only woman in China to rule as empress in her own right
q-asien-altertum-09#choices.3: She had the Terracotta Army made
q-asien-altertum-09#explanation: In 690 Wu Zetian proclaimed a dynasty of her own and is the only woman in Chinese history to have borne the imperial title herself.
q-asien-altertum-10#question: Why is the Diamond Sutra of 868 so important for the history of printing?
q-asien-altertum-10#choices.0: It was printed with movable metal type
q-asien-altertum-10#choices.1: It is the first book made of paper
q-asien-altertum-10#choices.2: It is the oldest surviving printed text bearing a precise date
q-asien-altertum-10#choices.3: It was used by Gutenberg as a model
q-asien-altertum-10#explanation: The colophon of the scroll, printed from woodblocks, gives the date May 11, 868; it is thus the oldest dated printed book in the world.
q-asien-altertum-11#question: Which empire did Ardashir I replace in Persia in the year 224?
q-asien-altertum-11#explanation: In 224 Ardashir I defeated the last Parthian king and founded the Sasanian Empire, which lasted until 651.
q-asien-altertum-12#question: Who wrote the Shiji around 100 BC, the first comprehensive work of Chinese historiography?
q-asien-altertum-12#explanation: The court historian Sima Qian wrote the Shiji in 130 chapters; Cai Lun improved paper, Zhang Qian was an envoy and Xuanzang a Buddhist pilgrim.
q-asien-altertum-13#question: Which state ended the Warring States period in China in 221 BC?
q-asien-altertum-13#explanation: The king of Qin defeated the six remaining states and called himself the First Emperor. The name China probably derives from Qin.
q-asien-altertum-14#question: Near which present-day city was the Terracotta Army discovered in 1974?
q-asien-altertum-14#explanation: Farmers digging a well came upon the clay soldiers in the First Emperor's burial complex at Mount Li. The actual burial mound has still not been opened.
q-asien-altertum-15#question: Against whom were the frontier walls joined together under Qin Shi Huang, the first Great Wall, meant to protect?
q-asien-altertum-15#choices.1: Against peasant revolts in the south
q-asien-altertum-15#choices.2: Against Indian armies in the west
q-asien-altertum-15#choices.3: Against nomadic horsemen in the north
q-asien-altertum-15#explanation: Steppe peoples such as the Xiongnu repeatedly threatened northern China. Most of the wall visible today dates from the much later Ming period.
q-asien-altertum-16#question: Which present-day city was Heian-kyo, seat of the Japanese imperial court from 794?
q-asien-altertum-16#explanation: Emperor Kanmu moved the court to Heian-kyo to escape the influence of the Buddhist monasteries of Nara. Kyoto remained the imperial city for over a thousand years.
q-asien-altertum-17#question: Who wrote The Tale of Genji, regarded as the world's first novel?
q-asien-altertum-17#explanation: The court lady Murasaki Shikibu wrote the novel around 1008 in Japanese syllabic script. Her real name is unknown; Murasaki is the name of a character in the novel.
q-asien-altertum-18#question: In which present-day country is the temple complex of Angkor Wat located?
q-asien-altertum-18#explanation: Angkor Wat was built by the Khmer in the 12th century as a temple to Vishnu. Today it is Cambodia's national symbol and appears on its flag.
q-asien-altertum-19#question: Who conquered the Persian Empire of the Achaemenids in 330 BC?
q-asien-altertum-19#explanation: Alexander defeated the last Great King, Darius III, and took over the empire. Persian culture and administration lived on under the Parthians and Sasanians.
q-asien-altertum-20#question: On what basis were officials in imperial China selected through examinations?
q-asien-altertum-20#choices.2: Their knowledge of the Confucian classics
q-asien-altertum-20#choices.3: The size of their payments to the court
q-asien-altertum-20#explanation: The examinations were meant to award offices by merit rather than birth. The system lasted until 1905 and was adopted by Korea and Vietnam.
q-asien-altertum-21#question: Which drink became the everyday drink of the people in China under the Tang dynasty?
q-asien-altertum-21#explanation: Under the Tang, tea gave rise to a culture of its own, complete with teahouses. Coffee only became popular in Arabia centuries later.
q-asien-altertum-22#question: What did the Chinese doctrine of the Mandate of Heaven state?
q-asien-altertum-22#choices.0: The emperor is immortal and cannot be deposed
q-asien-altertum-22#choices.1: A just ruler governs with Heaven's approval, an unjust one loses it
q-asien-altertum-22#choices.2: Only a monk may ascend the throne
q-asien-altertum-22#choices.3: The emperor is re-elected by the people every year
q-asien-altertum-22#explanation: Crop failures, disasters and revolts were taken as signs that Heaven had withdrawn its mandate. This also allowed successful rebels to justify overthrowing a dynasty.
q-asien-altertum-23#question: What was a satrapy in the Persian Empire?
q-asien-altertum-23#choices.1: A post station on the Royal Road
q-asien-altertum-23#choices.2: A province under a governor of the Great King
q-asien-altertum-23#explanation: The satraps collected taxes, raised troops and administered justice, but were watched by royal inspectors. In this way the Achaemenids held together an empire of many peoples.
q-asien-altertum-24#question: What did the Buddha proclaim in his first sermon in northern India?
q-asien-altertum-24#explanation: The Four Noble Truths explain suffering, its cause, its end and the way there, the Eightfold Path. The Ten Commandments belong to Judaism, the Five Pillars to Islam and the Five Relationships to Confucianism.
q-asien-altertum-25#question: Which group stood at the top of the traditional Indian caste system?
q-asien-altertum-25#explanation: After the priests came the warriors, then farmers and merchants, and the servants; below them stood the so-called untouchables. Buddhists and Jains rejected this hierarchy.
q-asien-altertum-26#question: Which city did Cyrus II conquer in 539 BC, after which he allowed the deported Jews to return home?
q-asien-altertum-26#explanation: After the fall of Babylon the Jews were allowed to return to Jerusalem; the Cyrus Cylinder bears witness to his tolerant policy. The Hebrew Bible, too, portrays him as a just ruler.
q-asien-altertum-27#question: What is meant by the Middle Way taught by the Buddha?
q-asien-altertum-27#choices.1: A path between indulgence and self-mortification
q-asien-altertum-27#choices.2: A pilgrimage route through central India
q-asien-altertum-27#choices.3: The midpoint between war and peace
q-asien-altertum-27#explanation: Siddhartha had first tried severe asceticism and then found the path between the two extremes in meditation. According to tradition he then attained enlightenment.
q-asien-altertum-28#question: In which work did Confucius' disciples collect his sayings?
q-asien-altertum-28#explanation: The Analects preserve Confucius' teaching on humaneness, duty and learning. They later became one of the classics every examination candidate had to know.
q-asien-altertum-29#question: Which political doctrine relied on strict laws and harsh punishments and became the foundation of the Qin state?
q-asien-altertum-29#explanation: Unlike Confucianism, Legalism relied not on morality and example but on reward and punishment. Its harshness contributed to the rapid fall of the Qin dynasty.
q-asien-altertum-30#question: Which war moved the Maurya king Ashoka to turn to Buddhism?
q-asien-altertum-30#explanation: By his own account, Ashoka deeply regretted the suffering of the war against Kalinga around 261 BC. Afterwards he proclaimed non-violence and tolerance in rock and pillar inscriptions.
q-asien-altertum-31#question: Under which dynasty did Confucianism become China's state doctrine?
q-asien-altertum-31#explanation: The Han ruled from 206 BC to AD 220 and trained their officials in the Confucian classics. Under the Qin, by contrast, Legalism had prevailed.
q-asien-altertum-32#question: Which goods travelled along the Silk Road mainly from the West into China?
